## Homeostatic stability of population dynamics

Under homogeneous initial conditions simulating a general population,
the model exhibits stable homeostatic mechanisms: population-level
metrics remain confined to narrow ranges across all 90 simulation days.
Mean perceived stress (PSS-10 = `r pop("avg_pss10")`, CV
`r pop_cv("avg_pss10")`, range `r pop_range("avg_pss10")`) demonstrates low
variability indicative of effective homeostatic regulation. Resilience
(`r pop("avg_resilience")`, CV `r pop_cv("avg_resilience")`) shows uniform
coping capacity across the population, and affect (`r pop("avg_affect")`,
CV `r pop_cv("avg_affect")`) exhibits controlled mood variation near
neutral. Elevated resource levels (`r pop("avg_resources")`) indicate
effective resource management through social network dynamics, and
moderate stress (`r pop("avg_stress")`) relative to baselines suggests
effective stress mitigation.

@fig-time-series depicts the longitudinal trajectories of all agents
across simulation epochs, showcasing stable temporal variation
indicative of effective homeostatic mechanisms. Drawing from
comprehensive agent-state data over time, this figure reveals
equilibrium maintenance through consistent fluctuations: population
metrics remain within constant ranges, affirming that agent-based
simulations can model homeostatic resilience via social network
dynamics, where interactions sustain mental health equilibrium without
excessive variability.

![Stable temporal variation and homeostatic equilibrium of agent psychological states across all simulation epochs](figures/full_model_time_series.pdf){#fig-time-series}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-model-level
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: "Model-level population statistics demonstrating homeostatic stability"
model_vars <- c(
  "avg_pss10" = "PSS-10 across agents",
  "avg_resilience" = "Resilience level",
  "avg_affect" = "Affect (valence)",
  "coping_success_rate" = "Coping success rate",
  "avg_resources" = "Psychological resources",
  "avg_stress" = "Current stress level",
  "avg_challenge" = "Challenge appraisal",
  "avg_hindrance" = "Hindrance appraisal",
  "avg_consecutive_hindrances" = "Hindrance sequence length"
)
mean_sd <- sapply(names(model_vars), function(col) sprintf("%.3f ± %.3f", mean(m[[col]]), sd(m[[col]])))
chd <- m$avg_challenge - m$avg_hindrance
mean_sd <- c(mean_sd, sprintf("%.3f ± %.3f", mean(chd), sd(chd)))
interp <- sapply(names(model_vars), model_interp)
interp <- c(interp, "Centered near zero, indicating equilibrium")
tbl <- data.frame(
  Variable = c(unname(model_vars), "Challenge–hindrance diff."),
  `Mean ± SD` = mean_sd,
  Interpretation = interp,
  check.names = FALSE
)
kable(tbl, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, row.names = FALSE) |> 
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = TRUE)
```

@tbl-model-level substantiates a homeostatic system sustained by social
network dynamics and agent interactions. Coefficients of variation range
from `r pop_cv("avg_resources")` (resource levels) to `r pop_cv("avg_affect")`
(affect), indicating tight population-level regulation. Balanced
challenge--hindrance appraisals (challenge `r pop("avg_challenge")`,
hindrance `r pop("avg_hindrance")`) imply neutral cognitive processing and
effective appraisal mechanisms, and the consistent coping success rate
(`r pop("coping_success_rate")`) across all agents validates the model's
capacity to simulate emergent equilibrium from individual interactions
that promote mental health outcomes.
